title: 338. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Scale Factors of Similar Figures
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the ratio of corresponding side lengths from a given scale factor.
questions.question: Two similar figures have a scale factor of \(3\). What is the larger-to-smaller ratio of their corresponding side lengths?
questions.explanation: The scale factor of similar figures is the ratio of any pair of corresponding lengths. A scale factor of \(3\) means each side of the larger figure is \(3\) times the corresponding side of the smaller figure, so the ratio of corresponding side lengths is \(3:1\).
questions.hint: Recall that the scale factor compares corresponding lengths directly.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the ratio of perimeters from a scale factor.
questions.question: Figure \(B\) is similar to Figure \(A\) with a scale factor of \(2\) from \(A\) to \(B\). What is the ratio of the perimeter of \(B\) to the perimeter of \(A\)?
questions.explanation: For similar figures, perimeters scale by the same factor as corresponding side lengths. Since the scale factor from \(A\) to \(B\) is \(2\), the perimeter of \(B\) is \(2\) times the perimeter of \(A\). Thus the ratio is \(2:1\).
questions.hint: Perimeters of similar figures change in the same ratio as their side lengths.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the ratio of areas from a given scale factor.
questions.question: Two similar figures have a scale factor of \(3\). What is the larger-to-smaller ratio of their areas?
questions.explanation: If the scale factor of lengths is \(k\), then the ratio of areas is \(k^2\). Here \(k=3\), so the area ratio is \(3^2:1=9:1\).
questions.hint: Area scales by the square of the linear scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the ratio of volumes from a given scale factor.
questions.question: Two similar solids have a scale factor of \(2\). What is the larger-to-smaller ratio of their volumes?
questions.explanation: For similar solids, volumes scale by the cube of the linear scale factor. Since the scale factor is \(2\), the volume ratio is \(2^3:1=8:1\).
questions.hint: Volume scales by the cube of the linear scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Find the ratio of corresponding sides from a given area ratio.
questions.question: Two similar figures have areas in the ratio \(25:9\). What is the ratio of their corresponding side lengths?
questions.explanation: If the area ratio is \(a:b\), the side ratio is \(\sqrt{a}:\sqrt{b}\). Thus \(\sqrt{25}:\sqrt{9}=5:3\).
questions.hint: Take the square root of the area ratio to get the side ratio.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the ratio of areas from a given side ratio.
questions.question: Two similar figures have corresponding side lengths in the ratio \(4:5\). What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.explanation: If the side ratio is \(a:b\), the area ratio is \(a^2:b^2\). Thus \(4^2:5^2=16:25\).
questions.hint: Square the side ratio to obtain the area ratio.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the area of a larger similar figure given the scale factor and the smaller area.
questions.question: Two similar triangles have a scale factor of \(3\) from the smaller to the larger. The area of the smaller triangle is \(5\text{ cm}^2\). What is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.explanation: The area ratio is the square of the scale factor: \(3^2=9\). Therefore, the larger area is \(5\times 9=45\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Multiply the smaller area by the square of the scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the volume of a larger similar solid given the scale factor and the smaller volume.
questions.question: Two similar solids have a scale factor of \(2\) from the smaller to the larger. The volume of the smaller solid is \(6\text{ cm}^3\). What is the volume of the larger solid?
questions.explanation: The volume ratio is the cube of the scale factor: \(2^3=8\). Thus the larger volume is \(6\times 8=48\text{ cm}^3\).
questions.hint: Multiply the smaller volume by the cube of the scale factor.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the ratio of areas from a given perimeter ratio of similar figures.
questions.question: Two similar rectangles have perimeters in the ratio \(3:5\). What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.explanation: For similar figures, the perimeter ratio equals the side ratio. Thus the side ratio is \(3:5\). The area ratio is the square of the side ratio: \(3^2:5^2=9:25\).
questions.hint: Use the perimeter ratio as the side ratio, then square it for the area ratio.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the square of a scale factor to find an actual area from a model area.
questions.question: A model car is built with a scale factor of \(1:24\) (model to actual). The area of the windshield on the model is \(5\text{ cm}^2\). What is the area of the windshield on the actual car?
questions.explanation: The scale factor from model to actual is \(24\). The area ratio is \(24^2=576\). Therefore, the actual area is \(5\times 576=2880\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Remember that area scales by the square of the linear scale factor.
